scope: Proposition 3.10 (Local component geometry) of the manuscript “Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2” (preprints/Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 010 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3c8797c7d468cdcc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The ring Ard is a flat complete-intersection normal domain over L, of dimension 1 + 8d, and its special fiber is a normal domain of dimension 8d. Set e = 1 + 8d + 4u + g. Then the following statements hold for the model (6). 1. Spec Bi is irreducible of dimension e, and its unique irreducible component is horizontal. 2. The two rings have a canonical common special fiber, compatible with their universal matrices and the variables X1, . . . , Xg. Its irreducible components have dimension e − 1 and are indexed by a choice, at each tame place, of the unramified component or the closure of the nontrivial-unipotent component. 3. The irreducible components of Spec B1 are horizontal and have dimension e. They are indexed by the same choices. The specialization of each has precisely its corresponding special-fiber component as underlying support. In particular the generic point of a special-fiber component lies on exactly one component of Spec B1. The assertions remain valid after finite extension of the constants and curve field and the resulting enhanced completion. No condition on the dyadic curve representations is required.
